planting.note: Nestle small divisions or spore-raised plants into shallow soil pockets on shaded sandstone or acidic rock outcrops; best in a dedicated rock or crevice garden with sharp drainage.

directions: Nestle small divisions or spore-raised plants into shallow soil pockets on shaded sandstone or acidic rock outcrops, replicating the crevice habitat this eastern native occupies as a naturally stabilized fertile hybrid between ebony spleenwort and walking fern. Its small, evergreen fronds range from simple lobed blades near the base to more deeply cut tips, giving each plant a variable, almost sculptural form. Best reserved for dedicated rock or crevice gardens with sharp drainage rather than typical garden borders, where it rarely thrives.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions shallowly in fall along shaded slopes, rock faces, or at the base of oaks, letting rhizomes spread naturally.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions shallowly in fall along shaded slopes, rock faces, or at the base of oaks, letting the creeping rhizomes spread naturally as this California and Baja native does over rocky banks and tree trunks in the wild. Growth is active during the cool, wet winter months, and fronds go summer-dormant in drought, so plan companion plantings that can fill the gap in the dry season. It makes an effective low, spreading groundcover fern for oak woodland gardens that receive little or no summer water.

planting.note: Establish divisions in fall in fast-draining soil or on rock faces within reach of coastal fog.

directions: Establish divisions in fall in fast-draining soil or on rock faces within reach of coastal fog, since this thick-fronded native normally grows as an epiphyte on trees and cliffs from central California north to Alaska within the ocean-spray zone. Its unusually thick, leathery, evergreen fronds tolerate salt spray and wind better than almost any other native fern, making it a standout choice for exposed coastal shade gardens. Use it on stumps, logs, or rocky banks near the coast where more delicate ferns burn or desiccate.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist, acidic, peaty soil at the margins of bogs, swamps, or shaded wet woods.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist, acidic, peaty soil at the margins of bogs, swamps, or shaded wet woods, the boggy, partly sunny openings where this northeastern native is typically found growing among sphagnum moss. Its delicate, upright, twice-cut fronds resemble New York fern but taper gradually at the base rather than narrowing sharply, and they turn an attractive golden color in fall before dying back. It is a good choice for rain gardens and consistently damp shaded low spots where many other ferns would dry out.
